# Capabilities

What ReScript supports, partly supports and does not support — methodologies, analytical procedures, qualitative research, question types and exports. Generated from the engine's capability registry (`packages/engine/src/capabilities.ts`), which reads the question-type registry and the analysis-method vocabulary, so this page and what Intelligent Mode is told cannot disagree. *Partial* says what works; *not supported* names the supported alternative.

## Methodologies

| Methodology | Status | Questions | Randomisation | Analysis | Chart | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Quantitative survey (descriptive / explanatory) | supported | single_select, multi_select, matrix_single, numeric, nps | option order (set_option_randomization), block order (create_randomizer) | frequencies, crosstab, chi_square, t_test, anova, correlation, regression | bar_horizontal, bar_stacked_100, mean_ci |  |
| Monadic concept test | supported | single_select, matrix_single | a randomizer showing ONE of the concept blocks (show 1); each block sets an embedded arm variable | anova, t_test, chi_square, crosstab | mean_ci, bar_grouped |  |
| Sequential monadic concept test | partial | matrix_single, single_select | a randomizer over the concept blocks, all shown, in random order | mean, top_box, crosstab | bar_grouped, dot_plot | concepts are rotated by a randomizer showing every block; the ORDER a respondent saw is not recorded unless an embedded variable records it, and within-respondent tests (paired t, Wilcoxon, Friedman) run in the Analytics workspace, not from the analysis plan |
| A/B (split) test | supported | single_select | a randomizer showing one stimulus block (show 1) that records the cell | chi_square, t_test | bar_grouped, mean_ci |  |
| MaxDiff (best–worst scaling) | supported | maxdiff_task | a seeded balanced design, versions assigned per respondent, task order randomized | maxdiff_scores, hb | maxdiff_utility | aggregate scores (counts and logit utilities) and individual-level HB utilities, both from the plan (method hb runs as a background job); the MaxDiff choice file is the hand-off for other tools |
| Choice-based conjoint (CBC) | supported | conjoint_task | a seeded efficient design, versions per respondent, alternatives shuffled | conjoint_utilities, hb | attribute_importance | aggregate logit part-worths, importances and simulator (logit / first choice / randomized first choice, revenue, WTP, demand, optimisation, segments) from the plan; individual-level HB from the plan (method hb, a background job) or Data Analytics; dual-response None (both codings) and brand-specific / labelled designs; latent-class choice models not estimated |
| Menu-based conjoint | supported | conjoint_task | a seeded design over the prices | conjoint_utilities | attribute_importance | take-rate counts; per-item binary logits with own and selected cross-price effects, a multinomial logit per exclusive section, aggregate and HB; menu simulator (take rates, revenue, price curves, bundles) |
| Adaptive CBC (ACBC) | supported | acbc_task | adaptive screening and tournament | conjoint_utilities | attribute_importance | BYO, screening (vs a threshold), unacceptable / must-have rules and the tournament coded into one model: aggregate logit + counts, and HB in Data Analytics; optional summed price (linear); simulator |
| Rating-based conjoint (CVA) | supported | conjoint_task | a D-optimal fractional factorial per version, task order shuffled | conjoint_utilities | attribute_importance | per-respondent least squares (optional monotone ties), R² and flat-rater flags, importances, simulator (first choice / BTL / logit); no HB (not a choice model) |
| TURF (reach and frequency) | supported | multi_select, matrix_single | item order randomized | turf | bar_horizontal |  |
| Ranking / preference order | supported | ranking | item order randomized | ranking_scores | ranking_bar |  |
| Constant sum / allocation | supported | allocation | item order randomized | allocation_shares | bar_horizontal |  |
| Van Westendorp price sensitivity | supported | numeric | none (fixed order) | pricing | price_sensitivity | the four prices are planned as one pricing item over four numeric questions in the order too cheap, cheap, expensive, too expensive |
| Gabor–Granger demand | supported | single_select | none (ascending prices) | pricing | demand_curve | a pricing item with method gabor_granger and one price per purchase-intent question, planned from the questions' own prices when they state them: demand curve, revenue index and the revenue-maximising price |
| Segmentation (cluster / latent class) | partial | matrix_single | battery row order randomized | factor, cluster, latent_class | segment_size | k-means / hierarchical clustering on a basis battery, and latent class analysis of categorical indicators (K compared by BIC), from the plan; no covariates in the latent class model; typing tools are not available |
| Brand funnel / equity | partial | multi_select, single_select | brand order randomized | brand_funnel | funnel_brand | the funnel (awareness → consideration → usage → preference) and conversion are run from stage questions over one brand list; composite brand-equity models are not |
| Key driver analysis | supported | matrix_single, single_select | battery row order randomized | regression, driver_analysis | coefficient_plot |  |
| Qualitative interview guide (self-completion, AI-probed) | supported | long_text, open_text | none (a guide flows) | text_themes | word_cloud | open-ended questions with AI follow-up probes, typed or dictated; themes are keyword-coded counts |
| Video / voice responses | partial | video_interview | none | text_themes | word_cloud | a video_interview question plays a stimulus and records a spoken answer, which is transcribed; dictation works on every open text field and grid text cell — the browser's recogniser, or (Firefox, or when it fails) a recording sent to the runtime's speech-to-text after the respondent agrees, metered to the project; video of the respondent is not recorded in surveys |
| Mixed methods (phased) | partial | long_text, single_select, matrix_single | per phase | text_themes, crosstab, chi_square, regression | word_cloud, bar_grouped | both phases are designed here (a qualitative guide, then the quantitative survey from its propositions) and recorded in the research design; nothing hands qualitative themes to the quantitative phase automatically |

## Analytical procedures

| Capability | Status | What works / the alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Frequencies | supported |  |
| Mean | supported |  |
| Median | supported |  |
| Top / bottom box | supported |  |
| NPS | supported |  |
| Crosstab / banner | supported |  |
| Chi-square test | supported |  |
| t-test (two groups) | supported |  |
| One-way ANOVA | supported |  |
| Mann–Whitney | supported |  |
| Kruskal–Wallis | supported |  |
| Correlation | supported |  |
| Linear regression (moderation, mediation with bootstrapped indirect effects) | supported | a mediation's indirect effect is bootstrapped (seeded percentile and BCa intervals) when planned with bootstrap |
| Logistic regression | supported |  |
| Factor analysis / PCA | partial | exploratory (PCA / rotation); confirmatory models are the plan's sem method |
| Reliability (Cronbach's α, McDonald's ω) | supported | McDonald's ω from a one-factor CFA beside α when planned with omega |
| Cluster analysis | partial | k-means / hierarchical; latent class analysis is the plan's latent_class method |
| Conjoint utilities | partial | aggregate logit (CBC, ACBC, menu item logits) or per-respondent OLS (CVA) with a market simulator; individual-level HB in Data Analytics (Hierarchical Bayes); no latent-class choice model |
| MaxDiff scores | partial | counts and aggregate utilities; individual-level HB is the plan's hb method |
| TURF | supported |  |
| Driver analysis | supported |  |
| Text themes / sentiment | partial | word / phrase counts, lexicon sentiment, keyword coding frame; AI-assisted coding with verbatim quotes is in Research Tools → Qualitative, not the plan |
| Ranking scores | supported |  |
| Allocation shares | supported |  |
| Pricing (Van Westendorp / Gabor–Granger) | supported | Van Westendorp (four price questions) or Gabor–Granger (method gabor_granger, one price per purchase-intent question) from the plan |
| Brand funnel | partial | stages read in variable order (awareness → … → preference) |
| Hierarchical Bayes (individual utilities) | supported | from the analysis plan (a background job with progress, started by Apply) or Data Analytics; CBC (incl. dual-response None and brand-specific designs), ACBC (BYO + screening + tournament), menu-based (item logits) and standard MaxDiff: HB-MNL by MCMC with convergence diagnostics (R̂, ESS, Geweke, acceptance), individual utilities, importances and simulation; no anchored-MaxDiff or CVA HB |
| Latent class analysis | partial | from the analysis plan or Data Analytics; categorical indicators: EM with seeded random starts, K = 1..8 compared by LL / AIC / BIC / SABIC / entropy, profiles and posterior membership; no covariates, distal outcomes or continuous indicators |
| Structural equation modelling / CFA | supported | from the analysis plan (the model built from the research design's constructs and hypotheses, each hypothesis read from its own path) or Data Analytics; lavaan-style syntax (=~, ~, ~~, :=): ML on the covariance matrix, expected-information SEs, χ² / CFI / TLI / RMSEA (90% CI) / SRMR / AIC / BIC, standardised estimates, indirect effects (delta method); no FIML, ordinal (WLSMV), multi-group or bootstrap |
| Multilevel / mixed-effects models | not supported | regression with a group control instead |
| AI-assisted coding of transcripts and open text | requires configuration | in Research Tools → Qualitative, not the plan; AI-suggested codebook, codes and excerpts (inductive or deductive), redacted before sending, every quote checked verbatim, human review (the plan's text_themes is keyword coding) |
| Paired / repeated-measures tests in the analysis plan | partial | paired t, Wilcoxon and Friedman run in the Analytics workspace; the plan's methods are between-group |

## Qualitative support

| Capability | Status | What works / the alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Live moderated video sessions (focus groups, IDIs) | partial | Research Tools → Qualitative → Live sessions: schedule sessions with participant slots and unique join links; the moderator runs the room from the Studio (waiting room, admit, mute, remove, spotlight, push a stimulus from the guide, section timers, back-room chat with observers, timestamped observer notes, optional live AI assist that never speaks); participants join from their link in the browser after a consent screen and a camera / microphone check; silent observers watch from the back room, invisible to participants. Media: built-in mesh WebRTC (no SDK) for small groups; LiveKit tokens are minted when it is configured. With consent each person's audio (optionally video) is recorded in their own browser, uploaded in chunks and transcribed per speaker into one session transcript for coding |
| Selected quotes in reports | partial | the qualitative report (Research Tools → Qualitative) carries reviewed verbatim excerpts with source, speaker and time; the survey findings deck and report do not |
| Open-ended questions (short / essay) | supported |  |
| AI follow-up probes on open ends | supported | up to 5 per question, gated by conditions; fixed wording or written by the AI at run time |
| Spoken answers (dictation) on open text | supported | on by default on every prose field |
| Recorded audio answers with transcription | partial | video_interview answers in surveys; moderated session recordings are transcribed in Research Tools → Qualitative (qualitative:session_transcription) |
| AI conversational interviewer (voice) | supported | reads the programmed survey aloud and takes spoken answers; the survey stays the authority |
| Theme coding of open answers | partial | word / phrase counts, lexicon sentiment, keyword coding frame; AI-assisted coding with verbatim quotes is in Research Tools → Qualitative, not the plan |
| Interview / focus-group guide (moderated study plan) | supported | objectives, protocol, timed sections with scripts, questions, probes and conditional probes, moderator instructions, ground rules, exercises, concepts, screening, consent and recording disclosure, segments, session plan; created and patched in Intelligent Mode; exported to Word |
| Session records (interviews / focus groups) | supported | date, moderator, participants and segments, consent captured, notes, observations, status — records of sessions run elsewhere |
| Session recordings | requires configuration | audio or video uploaded straight to private storage (resumable), played or downloaded through a 15-minute signed URL after an access check (Data view + contact details) |
| Session transcription | requires configuration | through the configured speech-to-text provider, with timings and speaker separation where the provider offers it (recorded truthfully) |
| Transcript import (.txt, .vtt, .srt, .docx, “Speaker: text”) | supported | speaker ids and timestamps preserved; moderator role and participant segment suggested and editable; open-ended survey answers can be added as a source |
| PII redaction of qualitative text | supported | e-mail addresses, phone numbers and a names list replaced before any AI call and for members without contact-details access; spans map back to the original |
| Human review of codes, themes and excerpts | supported | accept / reject / edit / merge / split codes, rename themes, reassign excerpts, add manual codes and excerpts (verbatim-checked), history of who did what when |
| Inter-coder agreement (Cohen's kappa per code) | supported | two coders (the AI can be one) over the segments both coded; disagreements listed; undefined when a code has no variation |
| Theme frequency, negative cases, representative quotes, evidence-based summaries | supported | frequency by group labelled as not importance or significance; every summary claim cites excerpt ids; sentiment only as a labelled lexicon reading |
| AI-moderated 1:1 interviews (asynchronous, from a link) | supported | an interview guide run by an AI moderator with each participant: consent, screener and quotas, the guide's questions in order with probing per question (none / light / deep), conditional probes, stimuli, objective coverage, the time budget, in the participant's language; text chat; transcripts land in Research Tools → Qualitative for coding; the researcher watches interviews arrive, ends or excludes them; scripted fallback when the AI is unavailable |
| AI interviews by voice / voice + camera | requires configuration | turn-based (speak, check the transcript, send) or a hands-free conversation (G1): voice-activity detection in the browser, each utterance sent at the end of the turn, the reply spoken sentence by sentence as it streams — each sentence only after the output checks — and the participant can interrupt (playback stops, the interruption is recorded and the moderator takes it into account); latency (end of speech → first audio) measured per turn; with consent each answer's camera recording is stored privately |
| Realtime AI voice | requires configuration | speech-to-speech through a realtime provider over WebRTC (server-minted ephemeral session): the guide as instructions, tool calls for probe / next question / check-in / end, every participant utterance through the engine's rules first, both sides transcribed and recorded, the provider's own words checked AFTER they are spoken (flagged, the scripted turn follows as a correction) |
| AI qual synthesis (summaries, insights, Q&A) | requires configuration | per theme: what people said, nuance, tensions, who said it by participant group, contradicting evidence; per study: key findings per objective and hypothesis ('not enough evidence' when that is the truth), surprises, recommendations labelled as interpretation, an executive summary, segment comparison, a journey / decision-driver framing only when the guide implies it and every stage is supported. Every sentence cites excerpt ids (checked); a sentence naming a group needs that group's evidence; numbers the evidence does not give are dropped; counts and coverage are computed by code. Versioned, editable (AI vs edited kept apart), stale when the coding changes. Questions asked of the data (route:POST /api/surveys/[id]/qual/ask) are answered from retrieved excerpts only, cited; nothing relevant = 'not enough evidence' without a model call. Recordings over 25 MB: see Session transcription (WAV / MP3 split without re-encoding) |
| Auto-coding of new sources | requires configuration | per study, off by default: segment → redact → code deductively with the current codebook (or propose codes) → AI-suggested for review → summaries marked stale (or regenerated); a resumable, idempotent, leased job per source revision; batched, metered, capped |
| Blind double-coding (κ and Krippendorff's α, disagreement resolution) | supported | a seeded x % of each source's participant segments; two coders (people, or a person and the AI) blind to each other until both submit (RLS keeps the private sets unreadable); Cohen's κ and nominal Krippendorff's α per code, pooled and mean; each disagreement resolved apply / do not apply with a note and history; agreed and resolved codings merged as reviewed excerpts |
| Highlight reels (quotes across sessions, clip playback, Word / PowerPoint) | supported | ordered excerpts with notes and a snapshot of each quote (changed / removed since is shown); a clip plays the excerpt's turn from the recording through a 15-minute signed URL after the playback check; the list exports to Word and PowerPoint |
| Transcript correction with history (excerpts re-anchored) | supported | a segment's words corrected (STT errors); excerpts outside the edit shift, inside it are re-anchored to the corrected words and flagged for review, deleted ones invalidated — a quote is always the exact text; every correction is a revision with before / after |
| Text group sessions (Remesh-style live conversation with many participants) | supported | participants join by link in the respondent app, answer each prompt in text and rate a sample of others' answers; answers clustered (AI, or by shared words without a model) and votes read by code (consensus / polarising); AI follow-ups approved by the moderator or, in autonomous mode, asked within the guide's limit after passing the probe checks; the closed session becomes a focus-group source with speakers and timestamps |
| Video group sessions | partial | live video focus groups and IDIs run in Research Tools → Qualitative → Live sessions (qualitative:moderated): built-in mesh for small groups, an SFU when configured; text group sessions (qualitative:group_sessions) stay text only |
| Live-session recording | requires configuration | with each person's consent, their own audio (and optionally camera) is recorded in their browser in short standalone chunks, uploaded progressively to private storage (resumable), transcribed per speaker (separate tracks: perfect speaker attribution) and merged by timestamps into one transcript (moderator and participants, with segments and clip pointers) that coding, synthesis, highlights and reports read unchanged |
| Live moderator AI assist | requires configuration | a side panel during a live session: the rolling transcript, guide progress (computed by code), suggested probes and follow-ups, and objectives not yet covered; each call metered to the project, the transcript fenced and PII-redacted; the AI never speaks in a human-moderated session |
| Live TURN relay | requires configuration | a TURN server relays media when two browsers cannot reach each other directly (strict corporate firewalls, some mobile networks); Cloudflare TURN (credentials minted per person through its API), static credentials, or time-limited ones minted with a shared secret (TURN REST) |
| Live SFU (LiveKit) | requires configuration | when LIVEKIT_URL / LIVEKIT_API_KEY / LIVEKIT_API_SECRET are set, rooms can use LiveKit for media: access tokens are minted server-side (HS256 JWT, node:crypto); observers join hidden and receive-only; the room logic (waiting room, admit, stimuli, chat, notes, recording) stays Rescript's |
| Scheduling live sessions, participant slots and invitations | supported | session times in a time zone, participant slots with unique join links (only a hash is stored), observer links, invitations and reminders by e-mail when e-mail is configured, waiting room, no-show tracking, status into the session records; also in words in Intelligent Mode (“schedule two focus groups of 6 next Tuesday 6 pm IST with Mumbai and Delhi segments”) as a preview card |

## Platform services and their configuration

Each of these works once an operator configures the service it needs; the platform page (`/platform`) shows whether this installation has it. Variable names only — values are never shown.

| Capability | Status | Needs | Configuration (environment) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Video / voice responses | partial | Speech-to-text provider, Media storage | AI_STT_API_URL, R2_BUCKET \| SUPABASE_URL | a video_interview question plays a stimulus and records a spoken answer, which is transcribed; dictation works on every open text field and grid text cell — the browser's recogniser, or (Firefox, or when it fails) a recording sent to the runtime's speech-to-text after the respondent agrees, metered to the project; video of the respondent is not recorded in surveys |
| AI-assisted coding of transcripts and open text | requires configuration | Language model | AI_API_URL | in Research Tools → Qualitative, not the plan; AI-suggested codebook, codes and excerpts (inductive or deductive), redacted before sending, every quote checked verbatim, human review (the plan's text_themes is keyword coding) |
| AI follow-up probes on open ends | supported | Language model | AI_API_URL | up to 5 per question, gated by conditions; fixed wording or written by the AI at run time |
| Recorded audio answers with transcription | partial | Speech-to-text provider, Media storage | AI_STT_API_URL, R2_BUCKET \| SUPABASE_URL | video_interview answers in surveys; moderated session recordings are transcribed in Research Tools → Qualitative (qualitative:session_transcription) |
| AI conversational interviewer (voice) | supported | Language model, Text-to-speech | AI_API_URL | reads the programmed survey aloud and takes spoken answers; the survey stays the authority |
| Intelligent Mode model reasoning (plans, generation from a brief, descriptive edits) | requires configuration | Language model | AI_API_URL | without a language model, Intelligent Mode is engine-only: instructions that name their objects still work |
| Plan-first execution engine (large generations, bulk edits and designs as small resumable steps) | requires configuration | Language model | AI_API_URL | a request whose predicted answer does not fit one call (100 questions, a bulk edit of every question, a conjoint study) is planned by a deterministic estimate into steps of ~20 simple / ~6 complex questions, each one model call checkpointed the moment it completes; the page drives it and the cron continues it with the page closed. Flags: COPILOT_TASKS (default on; off = single-turn as before), COPILOT_TASK_ADVANCE_MS (one page-driven slice, default 60000), COPILOT_TASK_DUAL_WRITE / COPILOT_TASK_RESUME / COPILOT_PLAN_RESUME (the plan-item mirror of the existing staged build), TASK_BATCH_SIMPLE / TASK_BATCH_COMPLEX / TASK_BATCH_EDIT / TASK_BATCH_LOGIC (batch sizes), CRON_SECRET (the continuation job). Durable only once migration 0074 is applied; before that the sandbox runs it in memory and a real project falls back to the single turn |
| Spoken requests in Intelligent Mode and Design with AI | requires configuration | Speech-to-text provider | AI_STT_API_URL |  |
| Machine translation of the survey | requires configuration | Translation provider | GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_API_KEY \| AI_API_URL | the Studio's translate button and batch translation; in Intelligent Mode the model writes translations itself (set_translations), so a copilot request needs no translation provider |
| Semantic retrieval over research documents | requires configuration | Embeddings model | AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL, AI_API_URL | without an embeddings model, passages are retrieved by keywords (BM25) — still cited by id |
| Transcription of recorded answers | requires configuration | Speech-to-text provider, Media storage | AI_STT_API_URL, R2_BUCKET \| SUPABASE_URL |  |
| Narrated video reports | requires configuration | Report narration switch, Text-to-speech | REPORT_NARRATION_ENABLED, AI_API_URL |  |
| Address search on location questions | requires configuration | Address geocoding | GEOCODE_API_URL | without it the typed address is kept and pins still work |
| Session records (interviews / focus groups) | supported | Supabase database | SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY | date, moderator, participants and segments, consent captured, notes, observations, status — records of sessions run elsewhere |
| Session recordings | requires configuration | Media storage, Supabase database | R2_BUCKET \| SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY | audio or video uploaded straight to private storage (resumable), played or downloaded through a 15-minute signed URL after an access check (Data view + contact details) |
| Session transcription | requires configuration | Speech-to-text provider, Media storage | AI_STT_API_URL, R2_BUCKET \| SUPABASE_URL | through the configured speech-to-text provider, with timings and speaker separation where the provider offers it (recorded truthfully) |
| AI-moderated 1:1 interviews (asynchronous, from a link) | supported | Language model | AI_API_URL | an interview guide run by an AI moderator with each participant: consent, screener and quotas, the guide's questions in order with probing per question (none / light / deep), conditional probes, stimuli, objective coverage, the time budget, in the participant's language; text chat; transcripts land in Research Tools → Qualitative for coding; the researcher watches interviews arrive, ends or excludes them; scripted fallback when the AI is unavailable |
| AI interviews by voice / voice + camera | requires configuration | Speech-to-text provider, Text-to-speech, Media storage | AI_STT_API_URL, AI_API_URL, R2_BUCKET \| SUPABASE_URL | turn-based (speak, check the transcript, send) or a hands-free conversation (G1): voice-activity detection in the browser, each utterance sent at the end of the turn, the reply spoken sentence by sentence as it streams — each sentence only after the output checks — and the participant can interrupt (playback stops, the interruption is recorded and the moderator takes it into account); latency (end of speech → first audio) measured per turn; with consent each answer's camera recording is stored privately |

Presets come from each panel's public integration material and must be verified with the panel's current docs; no panel API is called |
| Signed panel end links (HMAC-SHA256 / HMAC-SHA1 / salted SHA) | requires configuration | Integration secrets key, Supabase database | INTEGRATIONS_SECRET_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY | the end link signed with the panel's secret (over the URL, the query or chosen parameters; hex / base64 / base64url) so a participant cannot fake a complete; the secret is sealed with envelope encryption (the BYOK vault's scheme) and never returned to the browser |
| Alerts (AI-interview distress, abuse, injection, quotas, targets, cost cap, provider fallback, group flags, no-shows) | supported |  |  | per organisation and per study rules: which events go to which channels (e-mail, in-app bell, Slack, Microsoft Teams, a signed webhook), immediate or as an hourly / daily digest, quiet hours (distress always goes), a per-channel hourly cap and dedupe; distress alerts carry the study, the participant's pseudonymous id, a short redacted excerpt and a link to the live view — never full participant text or identity; every delivery logged with status and retries; a test button per channel. Without any rule, high-priority events go to the project team's in-app bell |
| Slack, Teams and webhook alert channels | requires configuration | Integration secrets key | INTEGRATIONS_SECRET_KEY | incoming-webhook URLs are secrets: sealed with envelope encryption and shown masked; the generic webhook is signed (HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + body, X-Rescript-Signature) with an idempotency key and retried with backoff |
| AI qual synthesis (summaries, insights, Q&A) | requires configuration | Language model | AI_API_URL | per theme: what people said, nuance, tensions, who said it by participant group, contradicting evidence; per study: key findings per objective and hypothesis ('not enough evidence' when that is the truth), surprises, recommendations labelled as interpretation, an executive summary, segment comparison, a journey / decision-driver framing only when the guide implies it and every stage is supported. Every sentence cites excerpt ids (checked); a sentence naming a group needs that group's evidence; numbers the evidence does not give are dropped; counts and coverage are computed by code. Versioned, editable (AI vs edited kept apart), stale when the coding changes. Questions asked of the data (route:POST /api/surveys/[id]/qual/ask) are answered from retrieved excerpts only, cited; nothing relevant = 'not enough evidence' without a model call. Recordings over 25 MB: see Session transcription (WAV / MP3 split without re-encoding) |
| Auto-coding of new sources | requires configuration | Language model, Supabase database | AI_API_URL, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY | per study, off by default: segment → redact → code deductively with the current codebook (or propose codes) → AI-suggested for review → summaries marked stale (or regenerated); a resumable, idempotent, leased job per source revision; batched, metered, capped |
| Live-session recording | requires configuration | Media storage, Speech-to-text provider, Supabase database | R2_BUCKET \| SUPABASE_URL, AI_STT_API_URL, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY | with each person's consent, their own audio (and optionally camera) is recorded in their browser in short standalone chunks, uploaded progressively to private storage (resumable), transcribed per speaker (separate tracks: perfect speaker attribution) and merged by timestamps into one transcript (moderator and participants, with segments and clip pointers) that coding, synthesis, highlights and reports read unchanged |
| Live moderator AI assist | requires configuration | Language model | AI_API_URL | a side panel during a live session: the rolling transcript, guide progress (computed by code), suggested probes and follow-ups, and objectives not yet covered; each call metered to the project, the transcript fenced and PII-redacted; the AI never speaks in a human-moderated session |
| Live TURN relay | requires configuration | TURN relay (live sessions) | CLOUDFLARE_TURN_KEY_ID (or WEBRTC_TURN_URLS) | a TURN server relays media when two browsers cannot reach each other directly (strict corporate firewalls, some mobile networks); Cloudflare TURN (credentials minted per person through its API), static credentials, or time-limited ones minted with a shared secret (TURN REST) |
| Live SFU (LiveKit) | requires configuration | SFU for large live sessions (LiveKit) | LIVEKIT_URL, LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET | when LIVEKIT_URL / LIVEKIT_API_KEY / LIVEKIT_API_SECRET are set, rooms can use LiveKit for media: access tokens are minted server-side (HS256 JWT, node:crypto); observers join hidden and receive-only; the room logic (waiting room, admit, stimuli, chat, notes, recording) stays Rescript's |
| Hidden questions (respondent-invisible, programmer-visible) with auto-punch visualisation | supported |  |  | Properties → State has one switch, Hidden (Read Only was removed; an old definition's readOnly flag is still honoured by the renderer). Hidden controls RESPONDENT visibility: on a live / published link the question is not drawn at all — no text, no options, no empty space, no page of its own — while its auto-punch, display / skip / branch logic, piping, calculations and carry-forward keep running and the punched value is stored. In the builder, the Studio preview, the runtime's test mode and on a test link the question is shown in a purple hidden-question theme (dashed border, eye-slash, HIDDEN QUESTION — TEST MODE badge, info banner, 'Q6 — HIDDEN' beside the number, 'Visibility: Hidden from live respondents' footer) on every question type, and a question with auto-punch rules shows the punched option(s) in green with an AUTO-PUNCHED badge, an Auto-Punch Status line (applied / waiting for condition / failed / no matching condition), the selected answer and expandable details (source, condition in words, target, selected option, TRUE / FALSE, status) — a manual selection keeps the theme colour. The mode comes from the route that served the page, never from a URL parameter. A preview resumes from the tab's stored answers; a change to a question's options, Hidden setting, punch rules or logic in the builder invalidates exactly that question's stored answer and the punched questions that read it (configuration fingerprints), and nothing else |
| Contains / In list / Between on open-ended answers | supported |  |  | The logic builder offers “contains text” only where text is typed (text entry and its subtypes, Text List fields, Text Matrix cells, text columns, Embedded Data strings) and, under its own name, “is ranked” on a Ranking. A single select, multi-select, rating or grid offers no Contains: a stored one keeps evaluating exactly as before, is marked needs update and offers the operator that names it (equals / has selected / is) with one click; the linter warns, it does not block deployment. Open ends offer “is in list” (the whole answer is one of the values) and “is between (numbers)” (inclusive, numeric); an answer of several comma-separated values is read value by value — every value must satisfy it, a value that is not a number fails a numeric comparison. Display logic, skip logic, branch logic, quotas and the Test condition panel share one evaluator |
| Default / piped value on every open-ended field | supported |  |  | Every field a respondent types into can start with a value — static or piped ({{Q1}}, {{ed.X}} …): the question (Properties → State), each Text / Numeric List field, each Text / Numeric Matrix row, each Constant Sum row, each composite cell or whole column, each Other — specify box. Resolved when the question is first shown, written only into empty fields, never over the respondent's own value; validation, numeric limits, constant-sum totals and storage are unchanged. A pipe that resolves to nothing leaves the field empty on a live link and is listed in a test note in preview / test mode; the builder warns as the token is typed. Empty box = no change |
